author: Rahul kp
title: Agricultural Income
hook: not every farm is a farm!
simple_words: Income from Indian land and basic work on it is agricultural and exempt; poultry or dairy alone is not.

definitions.meaning: Rent or revenue from agricultural land in India; income from agricultural operations on it, including making produce marketable; income from a farm building.
Building on or near the land, occupied by cultivator or rent-receiver as home, store or outhouse. Land is revenue-assessed, or else outside specified urban limits.
definitions.note: Letting it out for other use: not agricultural

key_points: ==Agricultural income== is exempt, but it can raise the tax rate on other income (partial integration).
Three sources: rent from land, income from operations (including making produce marketable), farm building.
!!Land outside India!!: not agricultural income; taxable only where Indian taxability rules reach it.
Processing beyond making produce marketable (e.g. sugar from cane) is business income.

rows: Rent from farm land in India
Tea grown and made by grower

insight.text: Land in India plus basic operations (or rent from such land) decides it; the word 'farm' alone does not.

memory_trick.explanation: Rent from Indian farm land, Raise produce by operations on the land, Roof of a farm building. Anything outside these three is not agricultural income.

steps: Rent or revenue from land? Agri
exam_tip: Partial integration: net agricultural income above ₹5,000 AND other income above basic exemption limit. Not for companies.

doubt.question: If agricultural income is exempt, why does it matter?
doubt.answer: For individuals, HUFs, AOPs, BOIs and artificial juridical persons, it is added for rate purposes if net agricultural income exceeds ₹5,000 and other income exceeds the basic exemption limit.

mistakes.wrong: Poultry or dairy farming is agricultural income
mistakes.right: Pure poultry/dairy has no basic land operations: not agricultural. Fodder grown on land is.

mistakes.wrong: Sugar made from own cane is wholly agricultural income
mistakes.right: Making sugar goes beyond making cane marketable, so that part is business income.

mistakes.wrong: Rent from agricultural land counts only if the owner cultivates
mistakes.right: Rent from agricultural land in India is agricultural income even if the owner does not till it.

mistakes.wrong: Any farm house let out gives farm-building income
mistakes.right: The building must be occupied by the cultivator or rent-receiver; letting it for other use is not agricultural.

applicability: Income-tax Act, 1961; A.Y. 2026-27 basis (tax year wording)
reviewer_note: Verify the 60:40, 65:35, 75:25 and 60:40 splits (tea, rubber, coffee cured, coffee roasted/ground) and the ₹5,000 partial integration limit against the rules for the stated basis. Section numbers deliberately omitted.
check_notes: Writer: Verify the 60:40, 65:35, 75:25 and 60:40 splits (tea, rubber, coffee cured, coffee roasted/ground) and the ₹5,000 partial integration limit against the rules for the stated basis. Section numbers deliberately omitted.

Checker 1: Definition 2 (Farm building): the wording leaves out the ownership condition. Correct version: 'Building on or in the immediate vicinity of the agricultural land, owned and occupied by the receiver of rent/revenue, or occupied by the cultivator, and used as a dwelling house, store-house or other out-building. The land must be assessed to land revenue or subject to a local rate; if not, it must be outside the specified urban limits.'

Checker 1: Memory trick explanation ('Anything outside these three is not agricultural income') and Key point 2 / Step 3 (basic operations required): these leave out the deemed case in Explanation 3 to s.2(1A). Income from saplings or seedlings grown in a nursery is agricultural income even when no basic operations are done on the land. Add: 'Exception: nursery saplings/seedlings are deemed agricultural income.'

Checker 1: Mistake 1 right ('Fodder grown on land is'): this is vague. Better: 'Income from selling fodder grown on agricultural land is agricultural income, but the dairy/poultry income itself is not.'

Checker 1: Table row 2 / Step 2: for clarity, say the rent must be from land in India that is used for agricultural purposes. Also say the sale is by the cultivator or receiver of rent-in-kind; a buyer who resells produce earns business income.
